reason: The Book of Esther presents models of leadership based on courage, strategic wisdom, and principled stands rather than humility in the face of criticism. Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman (וּמָרְדֳּכַי לֹא יִכְרַע וְלֹא יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶה) exemplifies standing firm in conviction rather than yielding humbly. King Ahasuerus is portrayed as vain and easily angered (וַיִּקְצֹף הַמֶּלֶךְ מְאֹד), not humble. Esther's leadership is shown through diplomatic wisdom and calculated action, not through accepting criticism humbly. The narrative rewards decisive action and principled resistance over deference or humility when facing opposition.
